hash_always_scope.rule: hash_always covers only what git does not protect
hash_always_scope.why: Where git tracks a store it is already the integrity authority — the blob sha is the hash, git status is the detector, git checkout is the restore. A second hash set here adds no evidence and goes stale on every commit, turning the audit into a false alarm nobody reads.
hash_always_scope.enforced_on: measured tracked-ness (one `git ls-files` pass per root, cached), never a declared field
hash_always_scope.refusal_target: hash_never — never sentinel_files, because a sentinel set includes the newest file and that changes with every commit
hash_always_scope.checked_after: the envelope, so a store refused on scale keeps reporting scale
hash_always_scope.unknown_rule: If git cannot be asked, git_tracked is null and the guard does NOT fire: refusing on an unproven suspicion would delete the only integrity evidence the irreplaceable stores have, on exactly the hosts where git is not there to replace it. Every store honoured on an unverified probe is named in git_tracking.

sentinel.selection: the 3 largest files plus the newest file, by relpath — except inside a git directory, where the newest file is by construction whatever the last commit or push wrote, so only the largest are taken; and except where the registry declares sentinel_newest false, which extends that same rule to stores the pipeline chain rewrites. When no selected row is under the hash cap, the largest candidate that IS under it is added, so no store is left with size-only evidence.
sentinel.chain_output_exclusion_rule: Per-store sentinel_excludes name paths the CHAIN (fec/run_pipeline.py) rewrites every run. Such a file has no byte stability to assert, so pinning it detects the chain rather than corruption. The files are still walked and counted; loss detection for them rides A2 file_count. Declared per store rather than per store-class so a stale declaration surfaces as a red A2b row, never as silent coverage loss.
sentinel.exclusion_rule: A sentinel is an expectation re-checked days later, so it must be a stable artifact. Build caches, temp files, locks and logs are rewritten by ordinary operation and would guarantee a false disagreement. They still count toward the store's bytes and file_count.
sentinel.git_bookkeeping_rule: Inside a git directory (the store IS one, or the path passes through a .git component) the index, refs, reflogs, packed-refs, the transient *_HEAD pointers, in-flight rebase/bisect state and the caches git regenerates are REWRITTEN by ordinary commits, pushes and fetches. Byte identity is not a property they have. Recorded here because the 2026-08-27 landing commit proved it: the picker chose .git/index and the mirrors' refs/heads/main, marked them content_stable, and the gate went red on its own commit and push.
sentinel.git_objects_still_eligible: Loose objects and packs ARE eligible: they are named by the hash of their own contents, so they cannot change without changing name — the immutability a sentinel wants. Known residual: `git gc` can retire one, which A2b reports; that is infrequent and is a real change to the store, unlike a commit.
sentinel.git_dir_detection: measured — HEAD file + objects/ dir + refs/ dir; never declared in the registry

policy.secret_rule: SECRET stores yield path, size and mtime only. Contents are never read, hashed, or archived; the guard raises SecretAccessError.
policy.durable_backup_rule: durable_backup is false system-wide: OneDrive is a sync replica, not a backup, and no other target exists on this host.

extinction.definition: What ceases to exist if Disk 0 fails, over the counted stores only. single_disk means no off-box replica of the LIVE path; the rescue split then separates what the 2026-08-26 off-box rescue already copied into the OneDrive-replicated tree from what it did not.

stores.note: Lock files, logs and .git are excluded from the walk on purpose: they mutate while a lane runs, and a hash set that churns every run is a check nobody can read. Declares hash_always ON MERIT and is REFUSED by the git scope rule: ~/.claude/glassbox is its OWN git repo and all 15 walked files are tracked in it. The scope rule is about integrity authority, not disk redundancy — that repo is still single-disk, which is what the extinction section is for.
